stories.title: A randomized trial of supported versus self-fitting over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults
stories.description: Over-the-counter hearing aids may improve access to hearing care, but the level of support older adults need remains uncertain. In this multicenter, three-arm, pragmatic randomized controlled trial at ten community health centers in three Chinese cities, 322 adults aged 50 years or older with untreated bilateral hearing loss were randomly assigned (1:1:1) to self-fitting (n = 108), primary care physician support (n = 107), or remote audiologist support (n = 107). Outcome assessors and statisticians were masked. The primary outcome was hearing aid benefit on the Abbreviated Profile of Hearing Aid Benefit at 3 months. Here we show that both supported models produce greater benefit than self-fitting, with adjusted mean differences of 12.20 (95% confidence interval 7.18 to 17.22) for remote support and 9.71 (4.74 to 14.67) for primary care physician support. Hearing-related quality of life, satisfaction, speech recognition and device use also favor supported care, and differences persist at 12 months. One participant in the self-fitting group died of stroke. No intervention-related serious adverse events occurred. At 12 months, incremental costs per quality-adjusted life-year gained are $167.16 for physician support and $361.17 for remote support. Structured support improves the effectiveness of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults. Chinese Clinical Trial Registry: ChiCTR2400086117. In a multicenter pragmatic trial, structured primary care physician or remote audiologist support improved the benefits and sustained use of over-the-counter hearing aids in older adults compared with self-fitting.

stories.title: Sudden collapse of ice mélange under increasing submarine melt at tidewater glaciers
stories.description: Rapid ice loss from the Greenland Ice Sheet is responsible for roughly 20% of global sea level rise since 2002. Almost half of this loss is moderated by the presence of ice mélange, which influences glacial calving and melt rates. However, the seasonal to interannual drivers of ice mélange extent and collapse are poorly understood. Observations show a spread of behavior for ice mélange in different Greenland fjords, ranging from seasonal collapse each spring over a few days to perennial persistence. Here we present an explanation of ice mélange seasonality and collapse using a coupled ice mélange-ocean model that incorporates both high-resolution ocean circulation and dynamic granular mélange flow. In multi-year simulations, we reproduce observed seasonal variability of ice mélange and characterize the mechanism of collapse. We parameterize the threshold for ice mélange collapse and compare this to observations from five fjords across Greenland. Our results show that perennial ice mélange, currently present at the majority of the largest glaciers in Greenland, may suddenly collapse when subjected to increased submarine melt, which would drive greater calving, glacier mass loss, and sea level rise. This study models the collapse of ice mélange in glacial fjords in response increasing submarine melt rates. It shows that perennial mélange today is vulnerable to collapse subject to increasing melt, potentially accelerating glacier mass loss.

stories.title: IκB kinase epsilon deficiency attenuates osteoarthritis-associated pain and synovitis with limited cartilage protection in complementary mouse models
stories.description: Osteoarthritis is a whole-joint disease characterized by cartilage degeneration, synovial inflammation, and chronic pain, yet the causal role of IκB kinase epsilon (IKKε) in these distinct disease components remains unclear. We therefore investigated whether IKKε contributes to structural joint degeneration, synovial inflammation, and OA-associated pain using complementary in vitro and in vivo analyses in IKKε-deficient mice. IKKε deficiency reduced c-Jun phosphorylation, decreased Mmp13 expression in primary chondrocytes, and decreased Ccl2 expression in synovial cells, whereas p65 phosphorylation did not differ significantly between genotypes. In vivo, IKKε deficiency attenuated synovitis and mechanical hypersensitivity in the MIA model. In the DMM + MCLT model, inflammatory and catabolic markers in cartilage were reduced, whereas no statistically significant reduction in histological cartilage degeneration was detected. IKKε-deficient chondrocytes also showed increased Ikkβ and Tbk1 expression, which may represent a potential adaptive response, although functional compensation was not established. Together, these findings show that IKKε deficiency attenuates OA-associated synovitis and pain-related behavior and alters cartilage inflammatory and catabolic signaling, while its effect on structural cartilage degeneration remains uncertain, supporting the potential of IKKε as a therapeutic target for OA pain and synovial pathology.

stories.title: Nuclear adaptation to intracellular mechanical forces regulates the phagocytic capacity of Drosophila macrophages in vivo
stories.description: How macrophages fine-tune their appetite to fulfil their clearance role is incompletely understood. Phagocytosis exacerbates cytoplasmic crowding, but whether macrophages can sense this increase and use it to regulate their phagocytic capacity has never been investigated. Here, we test the hypothesis that phagosomes exert a strain on the nucleus, which in turn responds to the intracellular mechanical inputs influencing macrophage appetite. Combining genetic manipulation and live in vivo imaging, we show that engulfed apoptotic bodies indent and deform the nucleus of Drosophila embryonic macrophages, and that phagocytosis increases Lamin B levels. Importantly, we show that silencing Lamin B or components of the LINC complex negatively regulates apoptotic body engulfment in vivo. Thus, we demonstrate that phagosome-induced nuclear molecular and mechanical adaptations are critical for Drosophila embryonic macrophages to sustain apoptotic corpse uptake, thereby unveiling a role for nuclear plasticity in the regulation of macrophage phagocytic capacity in vivo. Macrophages tightly control their phagocytic capacity, limiting intracellular overcrowding. However, the molecular details of this adaptive response remain undefined. Here, the authors combine live in vivo imaging with fly genetics and show that, in phagocytic Drosophila macrophages, mechanical and molecular adaptations of the nucleus to the indenting phagosomal cargoes are required to sustain macrophage phagocytosis in vivo.
